main_text.p: ximum emolumentum vertit. Deinde mortuo Antigono, quem vivum me-tuerant, defpectâ ætate Philippi regis, tum admodum adhuc juvenis, cum regnum aufpicaretur, ad ingenium re-deuntes Ætoli per Dorimachum & Sco-pam, cum nulla ipsis data causa esset, Achæos & reliquos Peloponnenses bel-lo turbarunt. Eo facto omnibus Græcis invisoqui quiete post debellatum Cleo-menem partâ delectabantur, bellum fo-ciale in se concitarunt. In id bellum, principe Philippo rege annū ætatis xvii tunc agente, quo cum amicitia ex con-ventione priore plurimis Græcorum conflabat, confpirarunt Achæi & eorū focii in Peloponnefo, Bœoti, Phocen-fes, Macedones, & qui iis cohærebant, itemque Acarnanes, Epirotæ, Illyrio-rum pars, omnes injuriis ab Ætolis læsi, & ob sacra profanaque passim violata iisinfenfi. Et tamen bellum hoc tam grave, & quidem magna animorum contentione gestum suftinuère Ætoli, Lacedæmoniorum & Elidenfium [?]amicitiā ac focietate freti, in annum ufque tertium fermè completum. Tan-tum gentis hujus robur erat. Pax de-mutuas clades variofque ca-tum jam utrofque, maximè verò malorum belli taederet, con-vênit

The text at the foot of the page is faint and partly lost; the lines from "Lacedæmoniorum" to "freti" are read with doubt, and "amicitiā" is marked [?]. The last word "vênit" is read from a damaged line and is uncertain. Printed text is set in roman with long s written as s throughout.
